facts.statement: Woodbinesuchus is an extinct genus of goniopholidid mesoeucrocodylian.
facts.quote: Woodbinesuchus (meaning "Woodbine Formation crocodile") is an extinct genus of goniopholidid mesoeucrocodylian.

facts.statement: Fossils of Woodbinesuchus were recovered from the Cenomanian-age Upper Cretaceous Woodbine Formation in Texas.
facts.quote: Its fossils have been recovered from the Cenomanian-age Upper Cretaceous Woodbine Formation of Texas.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Woodbinesuchus, SMU 74626, was found near the base of the formation in Tarrant County.
facts.quote: The type specimen of Woodbinesuchus, SMU 74626, came from near the base of the formation in Tarrant County.

facts.statement: The type specimen was discovered by Johnny Allen Byers and J. Maurice in May 1990.
facts.quote: It was found by Johnny Allen Byers (Ted & Mary's favorite boy) and J. Maurice in May 1990.

facts.statement: The lower jaw was elongate and slender, fused from the tip to the sixteenth teeth, and lacked a mandibular fenestra.
facts.quote: The lower jaw was elongate and slender, with the two halves joined from the tip to the sixteenth teeth, and there was no mandibular fenestra.

facts.statement: Yuong-Nam Lee tentatively assigned Woodbinesuchus to the family Goniopholidae.
facts.quote: He tentatively assigned Woodbinesuchus to the Goniopholidae.

facts.statement: Woodbinesuchus is classified in the family Goniopholididae.
The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Woodbinesuchus as Pholidosauridae.
Woodbinesuchus lived during the Cenomanian stage, between 100.5 and 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Cenomanian (100.5 to 93.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: Crocodyliform fossils are widespread in the Woodbine Formation where Woodbinesuchus was found.
facts.quote: Crocodyliform fossils are widespread in the formation.

rejected.statement: The type specimen includes the lower jaw, vertebrae, limb bones, shoulder and hip bones, and bony armor.
rejected.quote: The specimen includes the lower jaw and a variety of postcranial elements, such as vertebrae, limb bones, shoulder and hip bones, and bony armor.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'vertebrae limb bones shoulder and hip bones and'

rejected.statement: Yuong-Nam Lee named the genus Woodbinesuchus in 1997 and the type species W. byersmauricei to honor the discoverers.
rejected.quote: Yuong–Nam Lee named Woodbinesuchus in 1997, naming the type species W. byersmauricei to honor the discoverers.
